proposals: Each state finance department should publish its annual VAT collections on petrol, diesel and CNG as separate lines in its budget receipts, so the ethanol-blending shortfall, modelled here at about ₹17,863 crore at E20, can be measured from treasury data rather than estimated from assumed pump prices.

PNGRB should add to its state/UT-wise VAT case-study table the statutory notification and levy point behind each DPNG and CNG rate, so anomalies such as Punjab’s 14.3% CNG rate against a 3.3% DPNG rate, and Uttar Pradesh’s split input/sale treatment, are explained in the source itself.

PPAC should publish a single, dated table of petrol VAT rates for every state and UT alongside its state-wise CNG sales table, so states such as Odisha, Puducherry, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Madhya Pradesh can be placed on both sides of the ethanol–CNG package from one official source.

The GST Council secretariat should circulate a state-by-state estimate of petrol VAT foregone and SGST gained from blending at E20 and E30 before any agenda item on blended motor spirit or a compensation pool, so states vote on Option A or B knowing their own net position.

The public-sector oil marketing companies should disclose in their annual reports the contribution gain attributable to ethanol blending, so the margin Option B would redirect, put here at roughly ₹7,200 crore at E20, is a reported figure rather than a modelled one.
